findings.F1: Step 5's main measure is on the predicted side but close to zero. Across 404 non-overlapping breakout cases, the slope t of the 10-day excess return on the width forecast is 0.39. The top third beats the bottom third by only 0.0093 (Welch t 0.36), against a case-level standard deviation of 0.215 in the 10-day excess return.
findings.F2: The width effect changes sign across periods rather than sitting in one part of the data. The yearly slope t is −3.12 in 2021 (n 65), +1.72 in 2019 (n 44), +1.71 in 2024 (n 54) and +1.89 in 2025 (n 44), and it lies between −1.2 and −0.2 in 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2023.
findings.F3: The effect is not monotonic in forecast size. Mean 10-day excess return by forecast quintile, lowest to highest, is 0.008, 0.015, 0.058, 0.003 and 0.031. The middle quintile is best and the fourth is worst.
findings.F4: The sign depends on the horizon. The slope t is −1.49 at 3 days, −1.31 at 5 days, +0.39 at the plan's 10 days and +1.28 at 20 days (n 369). The raw width ratio behaves the same way (t −1.22, −1.23, +0.75, +1.45), so any positive width effect shows only at longer horizons.
findings.F5: No coin carries the effect. Per-coin slope t at 10 days ranges from −0.84 (LTC, n 70) to +0.79 (BTC, n 75), on 49 to 75 cases per coin.
findings.F6: Breakouts as a whole are followed by gains beyond holding, whatever the width. The mean 10-day excess return is +0.023 (t 2.14, n 404).
findings.F7: That gain is concentrated where the last 5 days' volume is above its 60-day level. In that half the mean excess return is +0.050 at 10 days (t 2.55, n 157) and +0.091 at 20 days (t 2.75, n 138). In the low-volume half it is +0.017 (t 1.10) and −0.002 (t −0.13). Width has no slope inside either half (t 0.12 and −0.04 at 10 days).

ideas.name: wide-range breakout, more coins
ideas.idea: When a coin closes above the high of its prior 20 days, the wider its 20-day range was against its 100-day range, the further price rises over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would favour upside breaks that come out of already-wide, active ranges and treat breaks out of tight squeezes as no better than ordinary.

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above the high of its prior 20 days, the higher its last 5 days' volume against its 60-day average volume, the further price rises over the next 20 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would favour upside breaks that arrive on a volume surge and refuse those that come on thin volume.
ideas.name: volume-backed breakout continuation
